recent_posts.title: Syntonic Dentiforms redux · Aras' website
recent_posts.summary: A developer revisited a 22-year-old Windows/Direct3D 9 demo called Syntonic Dentiforms and ported it to modern platforms. The port replaced D3D9/D3DX with sokol_gfx, FMOD with sokol_audio and stb_vorbis, and now targets Windows/DX11, Linux/OpenGL, macOS/Metal, and Web via Emscripten/WebGL2. Along the way, the author refactored the original codebase — reducing 24,000 lines across 216 files down to 6,000 lines across 49 files — by stripping out excessive abstractions, design patterns, and inheritance hierarchies that were common in early 2000s C++ game code. The result is a smaller executable and a reflection on how coding philosophy has evolved over two decades.

recent_posts.title: Rapidhash Unity port · Aras' website
recent_posts.summary: A C# port of rapidhash (a fast non-cryptographic hash function) for Unity/Burst is presented. The implementation is ~100 lines of code and uses Unity's Burst compiler for 128-bit multiply access. Performance benchmarks show rapidhash reaching 38GB/s on Ryzen 5950X and 67GB/s on Apple M4 Max, consistently outperforming XXH3 — especially notable since the C#/Burst port of XXH3 is 30-40% slower than its native C counterpart, while rapidhash's Burst port matches native C performance at larger input sizes.

recent_posts.title: Two years of Blender VSE · Aras' website
recent_posts.summary: A retrospective on two years of development work on Blender's Video Sequence Editor (VSE), highlighting significant improvements across workflow, user experience, and performance through versions 4.1 to 5.0. The small team of 3-4 part-time contributors delivered around 200 pull requests, with upcoming plans focusing on compositor node-based features, hardware acceleration for video encoding/decoding, and enhanced editing workflows. The post acknowledges audio functionality as a major gap and calls for community contributions in that area.

recent_posts.title: OpenEXR vs tinyexr · Aras' website
recent_posts.summary: A technical comparison between tinyexr and OpenEXR libraries for handling EXR image files. The analysis benchmarks binary size, source code size, and read/write performance across different OpenEXR versions (3.2.4 to 3.4.4). Results show tinyexr is smaller (251KB vs 649KB) but slower (6.55s vs 1.65s), while OpenEXR offers more compression formats and better performance. The post demonstrates how to build OpenEXR as a single compilation unit and provides options for reducing binary size by removing specific compression codecs.

recent_posts.title: Moving Blender video scopes to GPU with compute shaders for better HDR performance
recent_posts.summary: A detailed exploration of optimizing Blender's video editing scopes for HDR content by moving calculations from CPU to GPU. The author discovered that rendering millions of points using traditional GPU rasterization performs poorly on Apple GPUs, especially when many points overlap. Through extensive testing across 30+ GPU models, they found that a simple compute shader approach consistently outperforms built-in point rasterization by 1.5-10x, even with atomic contention. The solution improves Blender's scope performance from 1.1 FPS to 14.1 FPS while adding better HDR support and visual quality.

recent_posts.title: Lossless Float Image Compression · Aras' website
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive benchmark comparing lossless compression methods for floating point images with multiple channels, commonly used in film and VFX workflows. OpenEXR with ZIP compression remains the recommended choice, while the upcoming HTJ2K compression offers slightly better ratios but worse performance. JPEG-XL shows poor performance despite good compression ratios, making it unsuitable for this use case. Surprisingly, mesh optimizer combined with zstd achieves the best balance of compression ratio and speed, outperforming all established image formats by significant margins.

recent_posts.title: Voronoi, Hashing and OSL · Aras' website
recent_posts.summary: A performance optimization story about upgrading Blender's Voronoi node from a 1997 Jenkins hash function to a modern PCG3D hash, achieving 2-3x speed improvements. The work involved updating four separate implementations across different rendering backends, including working around Open Shading Language's lack of unsigned integers. The change required modifying the hash function from float-to-float to integer-to-float mapping to accommodate OSL limitations.

recent_posts.title: Blender FBX importer via ufbx · Aras' website
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the new FBX importer for Blender 4.5, which is based on the ufbx library. It highlights the advantages of using ufbx, such as ease of use, performance improvements, and its ability to read and parse FBX files comprehensively. The post compares ufbx's performance with other FBX parsers, showcasing its speed and efficiency. It also mentions the legacy Python-based importer and provides details about the testing and future inclusion of the experimental new importer in Blender 4.5.

recent_posts.title: US New Orleans Trip 2025 · Aras' website
recent_posts.summary: The post details a family's trip to New Orleans and the Gulf of Mexico coast towards Orlando. Highlights include visits to the New Orleans National WWII Museum, Whitney Plantation, Barataria Preserve, Battleship Memorial Park, Pensacola Beach, Alfred B. Maclay State Gardens, an airboat tour at Tohopekaliga lake, and Kennedy Space Center. Despite some challenges, the trip was filled with memorable experiences and reflections on historical sites.

recent_posts.title: Surface-Stable Fractal Dither on Playdate · Aras' website
recent_posts.summary: Rune Skovbo Johansen's Surface-Stable Fractal Dithering technique involves dither dots sticking to 3D surfaces with adaptive density based on view distance and zoom. The post explores the feasibility of using this technique on Playdate, a gaming console with 1-bit color screens and hardware comparable to a 1995 PC. Using this dithering technique on Playdate faces challenges due to limited hardware capabilities, making it impractical. Efforts were made to optimize the dithering algorithm's performance for Playdate, leading to significant improvements, though the technique remains heavy and shows increased aliasing at low resolution.
